utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Case number IT-95-16-T, the Prosecutor versus Zoran Kupreskic, Mirjan Kupreskic, Vlatko Kupreskic, Drago Josipovic, Dragan Papic and Vladimir Santic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Good afternoon. So we now resume.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Counsel Radovic. Examined by Mr. Radovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good day. Last time we came to the last question. This was the arrival of the displaced persons. We'll move to the next question which would concern whether you knew anything about the events of the 20th of October of 1992. If you heard about this incident, this would be the barricade on the road near the cemetery at Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: On the 19th of October of '92 there was a conflict between the Muslim forces and the HVO in Novi Travnik, which as a reaction to those conflicts, members of the B and H army placed barricades in Vitez and also at Ahmici close to the Catholic cemetery on the road. At 1.00 p.m. on that same day, the members of the BH army placed barricades in the region of Stara Bila, near the Bosna factory plant. The barricade remained up for one day, as far as I remember, and on the next day, the 20th, I think it was removed. I think that members of the HVO from Kiseljak, who were on their way to the frontline at Jajce, which in a serious situation then under attacks by the Serb forces, I think with the help of the military police they removed the barricade at Ahmici, and then after that the barricade in Stara Bila was also removed. This was on the 20th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that members of the HVO from Kiseljak and members of the military police removed the barricades, but would you please explain how they removed these barricades? Did they come there with shovels, did they move these barricades or was there any fighting in the removal of these barricades?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Since I was in Mosunj, which is opposite from Ahmici, so I don't know in which way this happened, but I heard that the barricades were removed. I think that there was some fighting. That's what I heard, at least.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us when you joined the HVO military structure?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: On the 22nd of December of '92.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So how did this come about and which section of the military structure did you join? Which military unit did you join, in what capacity and how long were you in that military unit?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: I went to the command of the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade, which was formed on the 22nd of December. The command of the brigade is in Novi Travnik. I was a political activist. I was the assistant to the commander for political matters of the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade. That's when I joined the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade is comprised of how many smaller units?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: It comprised two -- two battalions, members of the Vitez and the Novi Travnik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So these two battalions made up the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade. So who were the commanders of the two brigades?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Borislav Malbasic was the commander of the brigade and the commander of the Vitez battalion was Ante Bertovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So who was the battalion acting against?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Both battalions were acting -- fighting against the Serbs. We were in positions above Novi Travnik, facing Goles and Komar on the sides of Mount Vlasic. So we were facing Serbs and the Serb army. We were facing the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was the command of the brigade?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: The command of the brigade was in the town, in Novi Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you were in the command of Novi Travnik at that time?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I spent more time on the frontlines than in the command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So how did it come about that the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade was broken up or divided into two brigades?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: After three months the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade was transformed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just one moment. I asked last time for P1 to be placed -- so the aerial photograph showing this region. So if that can be put up again, please, for the witness to see. Are these towns shown on this aerial photograph or are they beyond the bounds of that photograph?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: No, they're not shown here. They're more towards Travnik, where the roads are. There's a road seven kilometres away that goes towards Travnik, and we were holding the frontlines near Travnik, to the west, for some eight to ten kilometres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So how far would this be from Vitez itself?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: From 20 to 30 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And now the question that I put to you: How did it come about that the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade was divided into two separate brigades, the brigade Stjepan Tomasevic and the Vitez Brigade, and how did this come about?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know the date exactly, but I think this happened in March of '93. That's when the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade divided into two brigades, the Vitez Brigade, and the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade which remained in Novi Travnik. Stjepan Tomasevic was comprised of members of the battalion from Novi Travnik, and the Vitez Brigade was made up of members from Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So how was the Vitez Brigade formed? What was the basis? What was the personnel that was included in that brigade?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: The command of the Vitez Brigade was formed first, and members of that brigade were part of the battalion that was in the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade. So in my opinion, and I would like to note that from the transformation of the brigade I was not in the command staff of the Vitez Brigade any more, I spoke to the commander, I asked him to return to sector 2 in Bila, because at that time the Vitez Brigade was divided into sectors, so I wanted -- so I -- the command of the Vitez Brigade was formed then. Members of the Vitez Brigade were members of the battalion that was part of the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade. I think maybe there were about 160.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So how many battalions should have been part of the brigade?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Four battalions, according to the structure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were a member of which one?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: The second battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where was your battalion deployed? We're speaking theoretically because it wasn't filled yet.

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I was in the region of Stara Bila. The command was located here. There were four of us in the command. This sector, the responsibility for this sector was from Zabilje through Stara Bila, Jardol, and then the second battalion took over after that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which battalion theoretically covered the region towards Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: The first battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did all of these -- should all of these battalions have been filled with members from the active component? What was the active component? And if they were supposed to be manned -- I will ask this first. I don't want the question to be too long.

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: The active component was included in the brigade, so it was filled with men who had signed contracts. They also received some kind of compensation. I think it was maybe about 50 German Marks per month. So the battalions were exclusively filled with men from the active component, but at that time we can't really talk about battalions. This was right at the beginning and it was unthinkable to have a battalion of only 40 men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would the witness -- could the witness see document P343? So this is an order by commander -- by Colonel Tihomir Blaskic from the 16th of January of 1993. Could you please tell us -- would you read the order and then tell us whether this order was, in fact, a call for general mobilisation, but read it first. Read it carefully, because your correct answer depends on the careful reading of the document. Yes, have you read it? Okay. Then you can reply to my question.

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Of course, you can't really consider this to be a call for general mobilisation. I can assume that the order was prompted by conflicts between Muslims and Croats in the area of Konjic, but I know from experience, since as a political officer I spent a lot of time with the guys on the frontline, so I know from experience that there were a lot of those who were not part of the active component who would go around in the settlements or around Vitez and Novi Travnik. Many of them carried weapons, and they probably got the weapons after Slimena. So the boys on the frontlines, there was dissatisfaction among them because they were the ones who were guarding the lines against the Serbs. They were working very hard, they had very short rest periods. So this dissatisfaction was a result of that. I think the purpose of this order was to try to include as many men with weapons as possible, to include them in the units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also read the introduction, the first part of this order where it says, "Pursuant to the order." Does this describe or give reasons why this order was issued? Please read it to the end. Why is this order issued?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: It was issued by the headquarters because of the aggression of Muslim forces all over the Croatian community of Herceg-Bosna, which has caused a lot of members to be killed, a lot of Croatian homes to be burned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us whether certain commands, commands of brigades or the command staff for the whole of the Central Bosnia, did they directly carry out mobilisation of the reserves or was this done through the office of defence?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: While I was in the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade there was no mobilisation, so with the transformation we went to the battalion. So this would be at a lower level. We went to the Stara Bila sector, so we could not carry out mobilisation. We were a battalion, so based on some information about people who had not been mobilised, we could provide this information to the brigade command, but the brigade could make a request to the office of the defence, and then based on that the office of defence could carry out the mobilisation, but within the unit we could not do that ourselves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if I understood you properly, the military structure passed on its request for manpower to the defence office, the defence office carried out mobilisation and would send men to that unit which had issued the original request. Did I understand that right?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, you did, but there was a department with the command of the brigade that dealt with personnel and structure, so then based on the issued call for mobilisation people would report to this department and they would be assigned to which unit they would report to and that's where they would go.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if you can please reply to the following question: This order, in itself, does that mean that the matters that the order pertains to has already been carried out, implemented?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: At the time when a lot of things were not implemented. I would call them irregular, extraordinary times, so every order could not have been considered to have been executed. Many orders were issued which could never have been executed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Prosecution document 341. This Prosecutor's document is related to the decision of the Croatian community of Herceg-Bosna dated November, 1992, on the setup of the home guard. So could you please tell me, first of all, do you know anything about this, namely, that in the area of Vitez there was a special home guard unit? So we'll take things one at a time. The decision was passed on the 3rd of November, 1992. During 1992 was any home guard unit established?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: No. During 1992 there could not have been any home guard units in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, until the 16th of April, 1993, were any home guard units established?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: No. There was only an active corps within the Vitez Brigade and also there were village guards that were not under the command of the brigade. So it is only the active part that comprised this unit. And, as regards home guard units and home guards as such, we can only talk about them from the period after the 16th of April when the conflict actually broke out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The parties presented quite a few exhibits, quite a few documents, that is to say that some kind of a regiment of the home guard issued orders on behalf of the Vitez Brigade. Did the Vitez Brigade remain as the Vitez Brigade throughout or did it end up as a home guard regiment?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: As it was transformed in March, 1993, the Vitez Brigade remained as such until the end of the war, until the end of 1994. It is only afterwards -- I cannot remember the exact date -- that it changed its name. Then it came to be known as the 92nd Home Guard Regiment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In addition to the 92nd Home Guard Regiment, on the territory of Vitez, was there any other home guard unit?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So practically this home guard regiment came into being on the basis of the Vitez Brigade; did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could the registrar please help me now with the set of documents, Prosecutor's documents from 340 onwards. It includes this set. It includes a document related to proposing certain candidates for posts within the home guards unit. It could be 341 or 342. Please, I would like to show this. This is one of the Prosecutor's documents that the Prosecutor showed one of the witnesses. Certain persons are appointed to the temporary home guard command in the territory of Vitez, that is to say on the 12th of March, 1993. On the assumption that on the 12th of March, 1993 a temporary command was appointed, that is to say of the home guard units, is there a theoretic possibility for this home guard unit to be set up within four days since the conflict broke out?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Of course not. In March, 1993, there weren't any home guard units in our parts. Later, in April, when the war broke out, we could only talk about the latter part of April.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am talking about the 16th of April.

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: No, not after the 16th of April.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So now look at the names of these persons who were appointed to the temporary command. Could you please tell me whether you know these persons. If you do, please tell me who you know.

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: I know the first person very well, Domin Matijanic very well, because he is my neighbour. I also known Nenad Santic, because before the war he worked at the gasoline station. Josip Maric, I think I know him too. He is from Vitez too. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since they were appointed to this temporary command, what do you know about this? Which military unit did they belong to when the war broke out? Also, what were their assignments and what actually happened to them? I am especially referring to the two persons you know.

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: I can only talk about the first person, Domin Matijanic, because he is my neighbour. I first heard of him being in some kind of a temporary command, because I was in daily contact with this young man. Of course, until the end of 1992 we were involved in the village guards together. I don't know. I don't know. I don't see that he could have done anything in terms of establishing the units. I didn't even know he belonged to this command. I'd really doubt this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where he was during the war and what unit?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: In the war he was involved -- he was not part of the active component, no. But I think after mobilisation, after the conflict broke out, he was engaged in our battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So he was in your battalion?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So he was in your battalion that was part of the Vitez Brigade, and he was not outside the Vitez Brigade?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: No. No, he was not. He was even commander of a company sometime in July, 1993 when our commander was killed. Then he took over the command of the second company of the 2nd battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of the Vitez Brigade?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know anything about Nenad Santic?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: No. Except that in May, I think, 1993, he was killed. But that is all I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he killed as a member of the Vitez Brigade or as the member of a home guard unit?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: As a member of the Vitez Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you don't know about Josip Maric?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: No. No. I just know about the postwar period, but I don't know what he did during the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now could we please have Prosecutor's Exhibit 335 shown to the witness. Could you please read the document first, carefully at that, and we'll later on move to the actual list of names. Actually, page 1 is of interest to me. So if you've read page 1 --

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: No, I haven't. Not yet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just put it in front of you. Please look at point 2 of this report. It says here that the Defence Office commenced the formation of the Viteska Brigade during combat activities. Does that mean that only when combat activities started that the Viteska Brigade was actually manned through call-ups, through mobilisation?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Of course. I said that the brigade consisted of members of the Viteska battalion that was part of Stjepan Tomasevic. That was the active component. In my assessment I said that I thought there were 160 of them, approximately, that is to say that one cannot really speak about the establishment of the brigade. The brigade was certainly established only after the conflict broke out. That is when mobilisation took place of these young men by the Defence department, and only then these formations were manned. Then the brigade started looking like what it was supposed to look like, only sometime in mid-1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. But do you agree with me that point 2 of this report, and this is a report that no one knew would be made public some day, this is an official report of the Vitez office to the higher ranks, that is to say the headquarters, that it is only when combat activities started that mobilisation took place for the Vitez Brigade?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: I agree with that. Yes, and that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I interrupt. I would like to raise an objection, because Mr. Radovic is always indicating what answer the witness should give to his questions. He is giving him every answer to the questions he is putting to him relating to this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Before I was the one who objected along these lines, and it is only natural that I should have them thrown back at me. All right. I am going to rephrase my question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you interpret point 2 of this report in relation to the beginning of mobilisation?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Until the 16th of April, that is to say until the conflict broke out between the Croats and the Muslims, one could say that only the command of the Viteska Brigade was set up, but that on the ground there weren't really men. So I would just call it formal letters on paper. So it was truly manned after mobilisation was carried out, after the conflict had broken out, that is to say, then, the brigade was manned to a certain extent. However, the formation of the brigade actually took place only in July, August, 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please look at number 3. It says "note" here. It says, "The formation of the Viteska Brigade did not progress according to the anticipated timetable." What is that supposed to mean? Could you please interpret this for us.

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Of course. Of course it could not have progressed according to the anticipated timetable. First of all, the period of time between the transformation of the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade and the other one was very short, and at that time one could count only on those young men who were in the active part, who were volunteers, who joined voluntarily and who signed contracts. In such times of war many people tried to hide and dodge the mobilisation. Even after mobilisation they dodged it one way or the other. So all of this made the situation increasingly difficult. Things could not have progressed as anticipated and during peace-time, for example.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I am going to read point 3. So I am not going to read the note, but the other one. It says here that most of the conscripts were mobilised and were involved in the first line of defence. They are used as replacements on the lines after the first assault, i.e. they are gradually included as replacements for the soldiers from the active component. Now, why am I asking you this? Why am I asking you to interpret some of these sentences? I am asking you to do so because the spirit of the Croatian language is different from the spirit of the official languages of this Court. So we have to interpret the exact meaning, lest there be any misunderstanding. Now, what am I interested in? We see the words that were used here in this report. Can we draw the conclusion who took part in the first assault, regardless of who had caused the conflict? So, according to the report, who took part, the active or the mobilised people? Please read this carefully first and then answer. That is point 2 under paragraph 3.

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Of course, as far as the first assault is concerned, it is the active component that suffered this, because we didn't have anyone else. We only had the active component that was at the frontline. We are talking about several days, and they were supposed to be replaced. Some of them were exhausted -- not some of them, all of them needed to get a change of clothes, a bath and to rest up a bit. That was the situation in the Viteska Brigade. However, in Stara Bila there wasn't any combat action, at least during the first few days we got all the newly mobilised, young men and sent them to Zabilje and to Jardol, that is to say to the left and right wings of our front lines. So somewhere there is replacements. The frontline was not fully manned from a point of view of quality, because we were not in a position to do so. There was very little resistance, I think. In the 2nd battalion, when the conflict broke out, I think we had about 80 young men, that is to say four platoons, and the line was about 11 or 12 kilometres long. So with this number of men we could not really cover the frontline from a quality point of view.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about these people, were they active or mobilised?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Active component. It was only the active people who were on the line on the day the conflict broke out. All of those people who were subsequently mobilised were sent to the frontline where there was combat action so that they could replace these who had gone through the first assault.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, please, look at the list of names that are included as an attachment to these documents. Have a careful look. You don't really have to look at the names, just look at the designations. To be more precise, can one see from this list who was mobilised on what day out of the persons on this list? Because, according to point 3, this relates to persons who were mobilised between the 16th and 28th of April, 1993, and in this list there is not an exact date when each and every individual was mobilised.

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: On the basis of this, of course, you cannot tell who was mobilised when. Actually, I see here that, for example, some people were probably never mobilised. It says over here by one person's name that he was absent, and this other person, who due too his age was not mobilised, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not really interested in that. I'm just trying to find out whether there's anything here showing who was mobilised when.

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: No. No, you cannot ascertain that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. That takes care of that. Now, tell me, do you know when did the members of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina set up checkpoints near the Bosna construction company?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: On the 19th of October, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that is to say the same day when this happened by Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any fighting there or not?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: No, there wasn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: I hate to interrupt, I apologise. I would like to ask a question still while we're with this document P335. I will ask this question so as to enable you to ask any question arising out of the matters which I'm now raising with the witness. Now, witness, I would like to direct your attention to the last page of document P335, the last page, just above the stamp. There is one name, Vidovic Ive Ratko, and above this in the English translation it's stated, "Did not respond." Now, what does this mean in military jargon? What is the significance of these words, "Did not respond"?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Let me just try to find this, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Last page. "Vidovic Ive Ratko."

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I found it, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Now, what does this mean?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. It says in the plural, but it's really one person we're talking about. I really don't know what is the case, but I imagine he was simply not there in Vitez, in the area of the Lasva River Valley. Perhaps he was in the Republic of Croatia, in Austria. So he had to be outside the territory of Vitez and that is why he could not respond to the mobilisation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Sorry, did not respond to the mobilisation. So the call-up. So he was not in a position to be mobilised.

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Well, he could have been in a position to be mobilised. For example, the defence department had records on each and every individual in Vitez, and those records date back to the old JNA days. So the records were still there and he could have been called up, but physically he was not in the area of Vitez.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: So could we then draw from this mention here the inference that except for a few others who were released, it is stated here, "Released, released, released," all these listed in this list were actually called up, were mobilised? Do you see what I mean? I'm asking whether we can draw from this mention, "Did not respond," the inference that all the other ones did indeed respond to the call-up and were mobilised, except, of course, for Vidovic Ive Ratko, as well as those in the list where it is stated, "Duty officers in front of the centre," and next to some of the names you have, "Released, released, released," and so on. Would you think this would be a logical and appropriate conclusion?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: That's right. That's right. On the basis of this, we can say that all the rest responded except for those who were freed for certain reasons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: You see now why I put this question, so as to allow you now to comment or ask questions in relation to my own question. Counsel Radovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, the witness's interpretation what this means did not respond. I did not think that it is proper, because obviously he doesn't understand administration. He didn't have much business with the administration during his lifetime. These words, "Did not respond," should mean this person was called up and did not respond to the call-up. That would be a proper administrative reply. I'm not going to ask him anything. I'm not going to ask him anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: You should refrain from commenting. Your comments are not appropriate.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think that Mr. Radovic, who is leading the examination-in-chief of this witness, should abstain from making any kind of comments on what the witness has done in the presence of the witness. The direct-examination is not over, and I find it very hard to listen to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: I agree. Counsel Radovic, please do refrain from making comments or asking leading questions as you did even after the objection by the Prosecutor. Let's move on. I apologise for interrupting you, and I wonder whether you would like to ask again the question you asked the witness before I interrupted you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: No. What the witness said in response was sufficient for me, so I don't want to make any further comments with regard to this list.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now tell me, do you know anything about this checkpoint by the Bosna construction company? For example, was it possible to move along this road, what kind of roadblocks were there, were there any victims, everything you know about this checkpoint by the Bosna construction company, please.

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: So on the 19th of October, 1992, a barricade, a roadblock was set up by the construction company of Bosna. It's not that I think so, I know that it was made up of vehicles, and you could, therefore, not communicate between Travnik and Vitez along this road. As a result of that, on this same line of communication about 200 metres away from that barricade towards Travnik, we set up a roadblock of our own. That is to say, of the Croatian people. There weren't any -- there wasn't any fighting. This went on until the next day. Then as soon as the roadblock near Ahmici was removed, the Muslims removed their roadblock and we removed ours. Perhaps it would be noteworthy, as I watched a CNN report several days after that, I saw on their film that there were quite a few persons unknown to me on that film. So it was not these Muslims who were from these neighbouring villages, but there were quite a few individuals unknown to me there. I didn't even know their faces. In this report I heard one of them speak, and I saw him too, of course, and he said, "We were not prepared for the Serbs, we were prepared for the Muslims." Later on when I talked to my friends I was told that he was a young man from Novi Travnik who happened to be at the roadblock there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know anything about this topic? Were there any kind of interventions by UNPROFOR because of the barricades?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know anything about the events around the Stozerac elevation above the village of Zabilje?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: The conflict that broke out on the 16th of April in the region of Stara Bila or Mosunj where I was on that day. There were no actions there, but the Stozerac elevation above Zabilje, that would be the left prong of our frontline.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you mean, "Our line"?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: The zone of responsibility of the 2nd Battalion. So the left prong of responsibility of our battalion. In the afternoon an attack was carried out by the Muslims. We had our positions at that elevation, we had a few men up there. So in the afternoon there was an attack. On the 17th, in the morning, the elevation was taken by the Muslims. Our forces were pushed back. So this elevation dominates over Stara Bila and Mosunj, Nova Bila as well, so it's a dominant strategically important elevation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know anything about the cattle farm by the Vlasic company?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: At the start of the conflict on the 16th, I know this farm -- on the 16th the Muslims were in the plants of the Vlasic agriculture company, and they were controlling the road from there, and communication was not possible on the Vitez-Travnik road for this reason, because the Muslims were in those plants.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know anything about the mosque in Grbavica?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: I know there was a mosque there. It's still there today.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any instructions -- it's a little difficult to ask this question without it seeming as being suggestive. Did you have any instructions on preserving this mosque?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: We didn't have any instructions. We couldn't have any instructions since the mosque was located inside the village of Grbavica, so deep behind their lines. So we couldn't really reach the mosque or guard it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's move to the 15th of April. What did you do on that day?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: On the 15th of April I was at home. Yes, I was at home. In the evening -- this was already in the early morning hours of the 16th of April. The commander called me to the command office by telephone, called me to come to Stara Bila. I think this happened between 2.30 or 3.00 a.m., and all the other members of the command arrived there too. We received information that an attack by the Muslims was expected. Then on that day, in the evening of that day, the attack on Kuber took place against HVO positions. The Muslims carried out this attack, so that an attack was expected. I was instructed, together with the commander of the platoon in my village, Mali Mosunj, to establish a line of defence in between the houses, facing the Muslims. So that's where I went, together with the commander. I engaged some men. We established points among our houses, at the border of our houses and Muslim houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say the commander called you by the telephone, which commander do you mean?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: The commander of the 2nd Battalion, Slavko.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when you came to the command, was the whole of the command staff there or not everyone had arrived at that time?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly whether everybody had arrived. I think there were four -- three or four of us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were orders issued to each person individually or to everybody together?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: To everybody together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please describe the premises where you received these orders? Who told you -- who issued the order? Who was the order -- who issued the order to the commanding officer? Could you please tell us a little bit more about what happened when you got to the command office?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Upon my arrival at the command, I think Slavko was there and two more members of the command staff. I think Marinko came later. The commander verbally told us all the information, that he had received orders from the command of the brigade for lines of defence to be set up, and also, he informed us that an attack by Muslims was expected, as well as information that already in the evening hours an attack was carried out by Muslims in the region of Kuber. We were also told at that time that the commander of the Zenica HVO, Zivko Totic, had been arrested together with his escort, that four members of the escort were killed, and I think there was an eyewitness, a Muslim, that Zivko was still being detained. So that was more or less the information. We were also worried by the fact that an attack will take place, and this required a seriousness in the implementation of our duties.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you stay at the headquarters?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: No. Afterwards, after about 20 minutes, I went to Mali Mosunj. I found the commanding officer, Franjo Antic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What level commander was he?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: He was a commander of the company, but we couldn't really talk about the company. There was really only a platoon in Mosunj, so he was a platoon commander. He had his -- he engaged the other men. I think by about 4.30 most of the men who had been engaged were already there. Then we agreed how to establish the defence points, where to situate them, and this is what we carried out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you conveyed to him what needed to be done, how did you describe the situation to him?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: I described the situation just as I had heard it from the commander, that an attack was being expected, that we were expected to set up defence points, and that simply the entry of Muslims to the village could not be allowed, because already behind our positions were homes where our families were, so we could not allow them to enter the village. Defence was our main task, exclusively defence, and this is what we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please tell us, before the 16th of April, except for this incident that you mentioned in Zenica regarding Totic and his escort, did you have information about other incidents that had taken place in that time period from January 1st to April 16th of 1993?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. The situation was being made worse with reports that Muslim forces had attacked the village of Dusina in the region of Busovaca, and I think this happened at the end of January. There was a massacre there, Croats were killed, and then I think after that attack against Dusina, as far as I recall, there was fighting for four or five days in Busovaca, which really never stopped after that in that area. I think there was some conflicts between Croats and Muslims in the area of Uskoplje near the Croatian village of Bistrica. I think Muslims entered that Croatian village. So I remember Dusina and then the conflicts in Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you know about Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: I know very little about Ahmici. I know what I heard after the events there had already happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you didn't participate in that in any way?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: No, I couldn't have, because Ahmici is in the eastern part of the municipality and Bila is in the western part. So it wasn't close.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So now a little bit about the accused. Do you know any of the accused personally?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: I know Zoran Kupreskic, Mirjan Kupreskic, Vlatko Kupreskic, Drago just by sight. Then I know him better now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's stay with the Kupreskics, because I don't want to go into matters that concern my colleagues. So I'm primarily interested in what you know about Zoran Kupreskic.

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Zoran and Mirjan, I don't know much about them because I worked in Travnik up until the end of 1991, so I didn't really spend that much time in Vitez, I was mostly in Travnik. But in '93, for Easter, so on the 11th of April, I was the president of the basic branch of Mali Mosunj. I spoke to my colleagues, so on that day, on Easter, we made a party on the Kalvarija hill to mark the Easter festivities, and this was supposed to be a party. We invited the cultural society from Vitez, and among the participants were Zoran and Mirjan Kupreskic. So we thought then that we could make it a tradition to organise such a party every year for Easter, and we wanted to have this party near the little church on the Kalvarija hill. But since it rained that day it wasn't possible to have the party there, so we held the fete near the river Lasva, in a Cafe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when you engaged the group, Zoran and Mirjan's group, were there several cultural societies operating in the region of Vitez or just that one?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: I think there were several besides -- besides there was -- besides their one there was also the Napredak cultural society, and I think Muslims had their own. I don't remember what it was called.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So let's stay with the Napredak cultural society. What was the difference between Napredak on the society Zoran was a member of?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: KUD existed earlier, so members of the folk dance section were of different nationalities, but I think in Napredak, it was mostly Croat. The members were mostly Croats.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear anything about a possible merging of these two cultural societies?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know. I just know that these two societies existed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When they performed for you at Easter, did they come -- were there members -- the members who performed were only Croats or did other members of other nationalities also perform?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: There were members of other nationalities too. There were Croats. I know one of them -- one among them was a Serb. I think his name was Veljko. He -- so a Serb called Veljko. This is how we can identify him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any Muslims?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, there were also Muslims. I know one of the Muslims. I don't know whether there were more than that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what that Muslim was doing in the folk dance group?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: I think he was in the orchestra. He was a drummer.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, I have completed my questions and I apologise for doing to the Prosecutor what he did during his part of the examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Is Counsel Slokovic-Glumac going to examine?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: I only have a few questions, since my colleague, Mr. Radovic, has asked more or less all the questions. This is our joint witness. Examined by Ms. Slokovic-Glumac:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kurevija, you cited in your testimony for Mr. Radovic to the point that you had placed strategic defence points in your village on April the 4th -- April the 16th. So what happened in the region of Mosunj on April 16th?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: On the 16th of April, in the region of Mosunj in Stara Bila, nothing happened. The lines, as they were drawn and maintained remained that way. There were no combat activities except for the odd shot, and this was probably done by maybe some curious people or out of fear. But there were no combat activities. But in the zone of our responsibility, the zone of responsibility of the 2nd Vitez battalion, in the afternoon of the 16th there were combat activities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please show us.

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: There were combat activities above the village of Zabilje on the hill. This would be the dominant elevation that I mentioned before. So in the morning of the 17th they took that elevation. There were also activities above the village of Jardol, which is exclusively Croatian. There is a village, Bukva, which is exclusively Muslim, so that village is higher up than Jardol. It's at a higher elevation than Jardol. So there were combat activities in Jardol. The lines were moved back and forth in quite strong fighting. But on the 17th, in the morning, we lost the elevation above Zabilje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in the region of Veliki and Mali Mosunj there were no combat activities. What about the region of Stara Bila?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: No, there were none.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the whole day on the 16th?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, on the 16th, the whole day and the next few days there were no activities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there were combat activities on your part of the line near Zabilje and Jardol?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: The left and the right prongs of our line of defence in our area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You stated that Croats lost that elevation, elevation Brdo.

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So please look at D42. D42/2. I apologise. This is an operative report under item 5. It stated that: "The part of extremist Muslim forces and also local Muslim forces from the villages of Preocica, Muratovici, Bukve and Putkovici, as well as a part of the forces from the village of Kljaka joined in a fierce infantry attack on the Brdo village where one of our smaller units is located; taking into account that the enemy was far superior judging by the number of troops and material and equipment, our units were forced to retreat in the direction of the Zabilje village." So this pertains to the loss of that village or that elevation of Brdo?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 17th; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that part of the line was your part of the line. Were there any Croats in that village where they say the village, but you are talking about the elevation?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: The elevation itself had no Croatian houses, no settlements, but some 200 metres below that the first Croatian houses began, and then, of course, people lived there. So at the elevation itself there were no houses, but 200 metres below that the first houses began of the Zabilje village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was anybody killed in the area of Stara Bila on the 16th and 17th of April?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: No. No. As far as I recall, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any houses that were burnt in that area?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Tell me, as regards the events of the 16th, how many men did you have when you said that you set up this defence line that did not actually operate that day? How many people were involved in this line?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: About 20 people, approximately a platoon, although not with a full formation, but approximately one platoon. We divided our 2nd battalion into four zones, four sectors, so there was sector Zabilje, that is to say the village is underneath the Brdo elevation, and then there was Mosunj and Jardol. So, in fact, as soon as the conflict broke out on that very day, we had one platoon respectively, approximately. Some platoons were better manned, others less, but approximately 20 young men, perhaps some people had 20, some had 25 or 26 young men. However, I think that the entire battalion had about 80 men altogether. That was the active component.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. One more question. When you spoke of these two roadblocks on the 19th of October, one was placed near Ahmici and the other one was placed near Mosunj by the construction company of Bosna?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you saw on CNN one of the men on the barricade saying something. Who was he, a Muslim or a Croat?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: On the Muslim roadblock all of them were Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So please tell me exactly what you said, because you said that this man had said, "We were not prepared for the Muslims. We were prepared for the Muslims (sic)." And that sounds pretty wrong, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Can you imagine what it sounded like to us?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But what did he exactly say?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: He said, "We were not prepared for the Serbs, but we are prepared for the Croats."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's right. And you said, "We are prepared for the Croats." I'm sorry, it was just a slip of the tongue then. I apologise. All right. One more thing related to the events of the 16th. In the part where you were, that is to say Mali and Veliki, Mosunj and Stara Bila, did you have any information or any control over the situation in Vitez and the surrounding areas?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: We did not. Of course we were preoccupied with the things that we were dealing with. There were combat operations in the area of Kuber, that was the 1st battalion, and I think that we then received information that there was shooting above Kacuni, this was also the 1st battalion, and Krusica, I think. That would be the 3rd battalion. Otherwise we did not hear anything more specific on that day, in those days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Is any other Defence counsel going to cross-examine this witness? Counsel Krajina? Yes, Counsel Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJINA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Examined by Mr. Krajina:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kurevija, I am Defence counsel for Vlatko Kupreskic and I am going to put a few questions to you. First of all, let us go back a bit to Prosecutor's document 335 that you spoke of a few minutes ago. Is it correct, and did I understand you well when you said during your testimony today that the Viteska Brigade was fully manned only sometime in July or August, 1993?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: That is when there could have been more -- higher quality manning of the formation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. In response to the question put to you, you said that as regards mobilisation mentioned in document 335, all persons who are on the list responded to it, except for those where it says that they were incapacitated or that they did not respond. My question, with regard to this, would be the following: On this list there are 489 persons. Do you personally know that in the period from the 16th of April until the 28th of April, 1993, over 400 men, individuals were mobilised in this brigade?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: No. No. I am not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Manning the brigade which was completed by the -- by July or August, as you said. Was it carried out by resorting to some other individuals or were these individuals from list 335 included?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: I did not say that the brigade was fully manned. I was saying that there was better quality formation involved. However, as regards this list, I can only judge by virtue of this very list that the others responded. But I cannot otherwise know whether they did or not. Perhaps I could have some knowledge as regards the 2nd battalion, that is to say those members from the list who belonged to the 2nd battalion. So it was just my conclusion that the rest had responded. And whether they actually did respond, that I cannot know. Could you please repeat your question once again. I seem to be talking too much and omitted to answer part of your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am trying to say that as regards the manning of this brigade in July and August, as you said, was it done by resorting to other individuals too or only the persons mentioned in this particular list?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: It was the defence department that got the necessary men, so I imagine that all of them were included in this list.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Once again, in your opinion are these only men who were mobilised after the 16th of April?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like to put a few questions to you related only to the accused Vlatko Kupreskic. In response to Mr. Radovic's question you said that you personally know Vlatko Kupreskic?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Well, not very well, but I do know him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you say whether Vlatko Kupreskic is in this courtroom today, and if so, could you tell us where he is and what kind of clothes he is wearing?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: He is sitting in the first row among the accused. He is the second one, if we look at it from the pillar, the second one on the left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of clothes is he wearing?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: He has a white shirt, a black suit, a necktie.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could the record please state that the witness recognised Vlatko Kupreskic. Mr. Kurevija, during your testimony on Friday, the 21st of January, that is to say before the weekend, you said that you are a member of the Croatian Democratic Community; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell me, when did you join the HDZ?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Well, from the very beginning of 1991, and at the end of 1991 I was elected President of the basic organisation, but I have been a member since 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So are you a member of the HDZ ever since then?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you hold a post in that political organisation nowadays?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which post is that?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: I am a member of the municipal committee and one of the three deputy presidents of the municipal community.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of Vitez?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, of Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether Vlatko Kupreskic is a member of the HDZ?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't know. Did you ever see Vlatko Kupreskic at some political meeting or did you ever hear him make political statements?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You did not. So now, Mr. Kurevija, I would like to show you a document. So could you please take a look at it and answer some questions that I would like to put to you in relation to this document. I kindly ask the usher to have these documents handed out to the Trial Chamber and to everyone else.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document is marked D18/3.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you had a look?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: I've read it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us now what kind of a document this is and who issued this document and who does this document pertain to and what is asserted in this document.

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: So this is a statement regarding membership in the HDZ of the B and H, and it was done at the Municipality Council of the HDZ of Vitez. It was signed by Mr. Dragan Vukadinovic, the late Drago Vukadinovic now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who does it relate to?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: It relates to Mr. Vlatko Kupreskic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Here it says, the basis of the records of the Municipality Council of the HDZ, that he is not a member of the municipality council of the HDZ Vitez and that he is not a member of the HDZ BH either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please look at the stamp and the signature on this document now.

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. I see them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, whose seal is this and whose signature is this?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: This is the seal of the municipal committee of the HDZ of Vitez, and the signature is of the late President Dragan Vukadinovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did Mr. Vukadinovic do?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. Vukadinovic was president of the Municipal Committee of the HDZ.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that he was the late Mr. Vukadinovic, that is what you said now. What happened to him?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Well, about ten days ago he had a traffic accident in which he was killed. He was -- yes, he was deputy minister of mining and energy in the federation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know him personally?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this his signature on this document?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it is. Mr. Kurevija, we have almost completed our questioning. On the basis of all these elements that you mentioned, the stamp, the seal, the signature, et cetera, can we claim with certainty that Vlatko Kupreskic was not a member of the HDZ?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: On this basis there is no reason to doubt it. We have records and I have known Dragan personally, the president, and I know that he never would have issued such a statement having not checked out the records, whether he was a member of the HDZ or not. So I have no doubts as regards to this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions. Thank you, Mr. Kurevija. And I kindly ask the Trial Chamber to admit this document as a Defence Exhibit into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: No objection from the Prosecution? It is admitted into evidence. I assume there are no other counsel, Defence counsel prepared to cross-examine this witness. So we can now take a 30-minute break and then we will resume with the cross-examination by the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Mr. Terrier?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Cross-examined by Mr. Terrier:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My name is Franck Terrier, I'm one of the members of the Prosecution team on this case, and I am about to put to you a number of questions that are directly linked to the answers you gave to the questions put to you during the direct-examination. When Mr. Radovic asked you if you knew the accused, you said that you knew Mirjan and Zoran Kupreskic well, and you said that you knew Vlatko Kupreskic and Drago Josipovic but not so well, you just new them by sight; right?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you don't know any of the other accused, right?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: I know Dragan Papic only by sight and Vlado Santic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You talked about Mirjan and Zoran's character and you also told us what you thought of Vlatko Kupreskic, but could you be a little more specific? How did you happen to meet Vlatko Kupreskic and what happened that made you know him in a closer way?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: I didn't know Vlatko Kupreskic so well. We weren't really that close. I knew Vlatko Kupreskic as a merchant from before the war, he was a businessman in Vitez, so that's how I knew him. I didn't -- we weren't very close.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A moment ago you were asked to look at Defence Exhibit D18/3. Maybe, actually, it could be placed on the ELMO again so everybody can have a new look at it. This is the last exhibit the witness looked at. When you looked at this exhibit, you said that you recognised the signature that appeared on the bottom of the page of the document, and you also said that you could authenticate the content of this document. So my question would be the following: How can you be so sure about the fact that Mr. Vlatko Kupreskic was never a member of the HDZ?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: I knew Mr. Vlatko Kupreskic. Not so well, but I knew him, as I said, as an excellent and well-known merchant in Vitez. As much as I appeared at meetings and gatherings of the HDZ, I never -- I don't remember seeing Vlatko there. I never saw him there. So in view of this statement, which was signed by the late Dragan Vukadinovic, the President of the municipality council of HDZ Vitez, I don't doubt whether Vlatko Kupreskic was not a member of the HDZ. I remember Dragan Vukadinovic, I trust him, and I'm sure he probably checked his records, and I'm sure he would not sign something that he did not check himself. So he probably looked at the records of the Vitez HDZ membership and probably, because he did not find Vlatko Kupreskic in these records, he probably issued this statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. I see what you mean. You held the person who signed this document in high regard, and this is what leads you to think that what is said in the document is the truth, am I right?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: (No audible response)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to put a new question to you. In response to Mr. Radovic's question as to whether you had heard about what had happened in Ahmici on April 16th, you answered that you had heard about what had happened, but you yourself were not in Ahmici when the events took place. You said you had heard about it. So could you please tell the Judges what you heard about the events which took place in Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Within the command of the 2nd Battalion, when I would report to the command occasionally, I think this happened two days after the conflict broke out. I think this was on the 18th. We heard that there had been fierce fighting in Ahmici. We had heard that there were a lot of Muslims killed in Ahmici, that there was a massacre there. This, of course, struck us deeply. So that's about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The rumours you heard about the events which took place in Ahmici, did you understand them to mean that a crime had been perpetrated, a crime which violated the Rules and Customs of War? Was that your conclusion?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: We were not informed in detail about what had happened, nor who were the perpetrators. But today, when I think about it, I am convinced that what you said is true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Today, with the benefit of hindsight, with the benefit of all the information you may have collected in the area, today then, do you have an opinion about who may have perpetrated these crimes?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kurevija, you said that very early on, as early as the end of 1991, you had joined the HDZ. I would now like you to tell us what it meant for you to become politically involved in the HDZ's activities.

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: I said I was a member of the HDZ, but not that I was engaged. I was engaged only from the end of '91. Within the basic branch of my village of Mali Mosunj, I was proposed by my neighbours and elected as chairman of the basic branch. So from then on you can say I was engaged in the HDZ. But since I was without a job at that time, I wasn't really active. I just worried and was concerned about the life conditions within the village, which was one of the tasks of a chairman of the basic organisation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would now like you to look at the document that I'm about to hand out to you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This document is marked 344.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kurevija, I'm not going to ask you to read all this document, I'd just like you to tell us if you've ever seen this document before. Do you know what this document is about?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: No, I haven't seen it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just by looking at the first page of this document do you understand what this document is about?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: It's an excerpt from the minutes of the meeting of the Presidency of the Croatian community of Herceg-Bosna, expanded to include Presidents of the municipal boards of the HDZ from B and H, the Presidents of the municipal boards from the area of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it is indeed the session of the Presidency of Herceg-Bosna, which took place on January 29th, 1992. Were you present at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: No, I wasn't able to attend.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kurevija, my aim is not to put you in a difficult position or to make you uncomfortable. Maybe I should have put my question differently. Your name appears. It seems that you were present at this meeting. So do you have any memory of attending this particular session of the Presidency?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: I did not attend this meeting. I couldn't attend this meeting. If you permit me to read it, I would like to see where my name is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please. You'll find it on the first page of the document.

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, it does state Rudo Kurevija, but I did not attend this meeting. I could not attend it. I assume this is a mistake. It's possible that it should have stated Franjo Kurevija. He was President of the initialising committee and he was a member of the municipal council, but I didn't attend this meeting. As President of the basic organisation, of course, I couldn't. With the post that I held, I couldn't attend this meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you are stating, aren't you, that you did not take part in this meeting, that you were not present? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: No. I did not attend this meeting. I did not participate in it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well then. The question I really want to put to you is the following, and in spite of your answer, in spite of the fact that you say you weren't present at this meeting I think I can put that question to you. I would like to you tell us what were your political aims? What were your political aims when you joined the ranks of the HDZ? You say you were not present at this particular meeting, so I'm not mentioning the meeting again, but, please, could you explain what was your view of the political activities of the HDZ during 1991, during 1992 and during the beginning of 1993? Please be as brief as possible.

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: In view of the fact that I didn't attend the meeting I can't speak about the meeting itself, but my political activities as the President of the basic organisation really involved taking care about the life within the village, in the interests and towards enlarging the number of the membership of the HDZ, and to increase the number of members within my basic organisation, to worry about the community needs, to strive at meetings of the municipal council, how to best resolve the current problems in my village and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as the situation of the Croatian community of Herceg-Bosna is concerned, did you have any personal political aims, or did you share some of the other members' of the HDZ's political aims? Did you have common aims?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Since I was not in a great position, having lost my job and I have -- having a family and three kids which I had to feed, my goals in life were to feed my family, and the political goals were secondary to that. So I didn't really think much about that. I really took care of my family first, my neighbours. I wasn't politically engaged very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Maybe I am mistaken, but I think you said in direct-examination that you had joined a military unit, the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade in Travnik, and I think you also said that you were the political head of this military unit. Is that right or am I mistaken?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: You are right. This was on the 22nd of December, 1992, when I was proposed to be a member of the command, and I was proposed as deputy commander for political issues, for political affairs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Precisely. Could you tell us what this involves, what it involved at that particular time in that part of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and what did it mean for you to be deputy head for political affairs?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Mostly it involved matters pertaining to the morale of the soldiers, seeing to all the needs of the soldiers on the frontlines. This is how I understood my duties and how I spent my time, mostly with the soldiers on the frontlines. But then having understood that this was too much for me, after the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade transformed itself or split into the Vitez Brigade and the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade, I spoke to my commander and he enabled me to be deputy commander, so to have lower rank in the 2nd Battalion, and they engaged another person to be the deputy commander for political affairs of the brigade. I couldn't really discharge all those duties. I'm apolitical, so at my request the commander made it possible for me to return to the battalion, and as I said, they placed another person at that post.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. Let's go back now to the situation that prevailed in the area before the 16th of April and on that date. Like many other witnesses who came before this Trial Chamber, you gave us the impression that the conflict started on April 16th, 1993, and it seemed that before that date, a relative peace reigned in the region. But you also noted that a number of incidents had taken place before that particular date, conflicts which involved Croats and Muslims living in the area. Some of these incidents were very serious ones. My question is the following: In view of these incidents which took place and which involved Muslim and Croats, and which took place before April 16th, 1993, and in view of the fact that some of these incidents were very serious ones, which measures were taken by the military authorities of the HVO in order to ensure the security of the Croatian community of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Before the conflicts of the 16th of April, of course there were incidents, unfortunately, between Muslims and Croats, but then right until the 16th of April we were on the frontlines turned towards the Serbs. So on that day, the 16th of April, we had our units above Novi Travnik. The region of Stara Bila did not record any particular incidents until the 19th, the matter of the elevation. Then even later, information shows that that place was a little quieter than the other areas. So on the 16th of April, the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade was being structured gradually. The active component was within it, and as far as Muslims themselves, at least in our region, there were no particular actions, no particular preparations, as far as I know, because there were no conflicts. So there was no need for any special activity there in that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Maybe I am mistaken, and if I am mistaken, please correct me. But if I am not mistaken, no particular measures were taken in order to ensure by way of military means the security of the Croatian community of Lasva Valley area?
