Nothing was done to prevent Muslim taking violent action against members of the Croatian community that lived in the area? Is that right or am I mistaken?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know if you are mistaken, because you are talking about the community of Herceg-Bosna and the broader region, Central Bosnia. I am speaking about Stara Bila and the place where I lived, where I was -- so I can talk about that. I don't know whether anything was being done in the wider territory. I had no part in that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are quite right to add what you just have added. Maybe I was not specific enough. I am talking about the Lasva Valley area, I am talking about the area around Vitez, and I am talking about the Croatian community who lived in this area. I am talking about the security of the members of this community. I am talking about incidents which took place in this particular area. So I'll put the question to you once again and I'll try to be more specific. In view of incidents which you have mentioned, which measures were taken, if any, by the military authorities of the HVO to ensure the security and the safety of the Croatian community living in the Lasva Valley area?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: It's possible that this was one of the reasons for the transformation of the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade to separate the brigades and to return the command of the Vitez Brigade to Vitez and to form a Vitez Brigade. Probably -- not probably there were attempts to man it with more quality. So possibly these were the reasons to ensure and to defend the Croats in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would ask that Prosecutor Exhibit 343 be presented to the witness, please. I think the witness had a look at it earlier on. Do you remember seeing this document before the break?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On January 16th, 1993, who signed this document, this order rather, in view of the situation prevailing in the area, that asks the combat capacity of all HVO formations in the area be put at maximum level. If you can, could you please tell us what military formations the HVO had present in the area at that particular time. I am still talking of the Lasva Valley area, I am still talking about Vitez, as you may well imagine.

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: At that time the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade was there comprised by the Vitez battalion. Of course the Novi Travnik and Vitez battalions comprised it. Then there were the Vitez formations. And that's as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the home guards? Was it considered to be a combat unit?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: No, they weren't and they couldn't have been considered as combat units. They were self-organised and were comprised of the population from the villages. How could they have been considered to be combat units when they were unarmed?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would ask that the Prosecutor ask more specific questions of the witness because -- is he asking about the village guards or the home guards? These are different things. The witness at no point equated the village guards and the home guards, so questions need to be asked separately about the home guards or the village guards. Also, the question needs to be asked whether the home guard and the village guard are one in the same thing. So I would like this to be clarified.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like Prosecution Exhibit 341 to be handed out to the witness, because it is true that it's not very clear what names should be used in reference to that particular unit to another. Mr. Kurevija, you've seen this document before, I believe?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is a document dated November, 1992. It is signed by the president of the Croatian community of Herceg-Bosna. Could you please explain to us, so that no doubt remains, could you please explain to us what units are mentioned in this document?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: This decision was passed on the structure of the home guard, the 3rd of November, 1992, that is when the decision was passed. However, this is mere letters on paper, because this is before the very inception of the home guard. They could not have actually been set up. There were only some working units. So within the working units they also belonged to HVO units. After this, I think that quite a bit of time had gone by before the home guard was actually established, that is to say before the 16th of April. That's to say before the conflict there could not have been a real home guard. That is to say that there were units that consisted of young men who signed contracts, and they were the active part of the units. The home guards came in only later, after mobilisation. It is only then that home guards came to the units. So after mobilisation they were treated as home guards. So they are home guards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I've understood you well, this is a national unit, it's not a village unit, it's not a unit similar to the one you mentioned before?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Village guards, those were persons within a village who had self-organised themselves, with the purpose of protecting the village from crime and any other negative development. And then the volunteers grew out of these village guards. They signed contracts and they become the active component and they were the first members of the HVO -- rather, I'm sorry, the Vitez Brigade. The home guard came only later, when the conflict broke out on the 16th of April, 1993. Then these persons were mobilised subsequently. They did not sign any contracts, because there was mobilisation then. That is when the home guards came in, so you can consider them to be home guards, whereas the active component consisted of the young men who signed contracts, they were paid in a way, 50 Deutschemark per month, as I mentioned. They were not members of the home guard. They were volunteers. They belonged to the active component, whereas the home guard were those who were mobilised subsequently.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree with me if I said, in view of the document that you have in your hands, that the National Guard is a unit that works on a territorial basis, and that it is a unit that is made up, in a sense, of reserve forces from the Herceg-Bosna military forces?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So should we understand this National Guard to be the structure who took the succession of the village guards, which you mentioned a moment ago?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: I don't understand. I don't understand. What do you mean successors of the village guard?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There is, on the one hand, the village guard, you've mentioned that, and on the other hand we have this National Guard. Is there not a direct link between these two guards? Is it not the village guard that became later on the home guard?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Well, the village guard was not in charge of itself. They were organised on their own within a settlement. However, the home guard, after all, did become part of the Vitez Brigade, and above them was a command structure, headquarters, et cetera. But, of course, the home guards were engaged from the village guards, and also from the ranks of those who were never part of the village guards. So all military-age men actually took part.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Maybe I should put my question in a different way. When the National Guard came into being, did the village guards continue to exist or not? Do you understand my question?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: The village guards did exist even when the home guards came into being. The home guards came into being after the conflict, whereas the village guards were there too. It is mostly elderly individuals who were in villages. They remained as the village guards. They could not go to the frontline, for example. And, as regards the home guard, we can only talk about it in 1994, when the home guard regiment came into being.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you be a little more specific as to the precise moment these units of home guards started to operate?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Well, a few days after the conflict broke out, that is when the mobilisation took place, and it is only then that we can talk about home guards, because that is when they actually came into being. A few days after the conflict broke out, I consider everyone to be home guards, because even those who were involved until then, I am referring to the active component, all of them were engaged at the frontline. So there is no difference between the active component, on the one hand, and the home guard, on the other hand, because the active component was paid until then. But during the war they could not have been paid.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The soldiers who were members of these territorial units, did they receive any military training?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: No. No, there wasn't enough time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of weapon did they use?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Well, they used what they had. By then there were quite a few people who did not belong to the active component of the armed forces and who had weapons. However, as the conflict broke out, we cannot say that all the members of units had weapons at that time. Weapons were mainly kept at the frontline, so then when new shifts came in, then men would give each other weapons before one group went home and the other group stayed. So the weapons remained at the frontline. They were not taken home. So there wasn't anything special except at the frontline itself when one had to know who took and who gave weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are talking about the frontline against the Serbs, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: The frontline against the Muslims. There were no home guards engaged against the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us now talk about the events which took place in October, 1993, in the Lasva Valley area. You told us about this roadblock which was set on the road going from Busovaca to Vitez, a roadblock which was established near the cemetery. I believe you said you were not present in Ahmici on the day the roadblock was established. You told us that the military convoy, interrupted by this roadblock, was going towards the frontline. How can you be so sure about that?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: The checkpoint was put up by Ahmici near the Catholic cemetery, but then there was another one that was put up by the Muslims in the area of Stara Bila. So we knew about both checkpoints and we received information the next day when the roadblock was removed from Stara Bila, that the unit that had started out from Kiseljak towards Jajce together with the military police, that they removed that roadblock over there and that this led to the removal of the checkpoint at Stara Bila. I had heard this information. Of course I was not down there, nor could I have been down there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I've understood you well. But my question was the following: Where were these HVO units going, these units which found themselves blocked by this roadblock?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: I already said so. Jajce.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I've understood you, and my question is the following: How can you be so sure about that? How can you be so sure this military unit was going towards Jajce? Did you get any personal information about that?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. I heard about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why do you think the Muslims tried to prevent HVO military units to go on the frontline against the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: I never said that they tried to stop the units from reaching Jajce. I think that these roadblocks were due to the fighting in Novi Travnik, right, so I imagine that the same goes for the checkpoint at Stara Bila. Not at a single point in time did I say that they had set up the roadblock so that the units from Kiseljak could not pass to Jajce.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why was this roadblock established, then?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Perhaps in response to the fighting between the Muslims and the Croats in Novi Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kurevija, I am now interested by the events which took place on April 15th, 1993. You told us that you had spent that day at home. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: You understood that right, yes, I was at home in the evening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you watch TV during the day?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: I do not recall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't remember -- I mean other than the events which took place in the evening, you don't remember that any particular events took place that day, events of which you would have been informed via the radio, via the television or via what neighbours may have told you?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Apart from the information I received when I had reached headquarters, that they had apprehended Totic in Zenica, and apart from the attack on Kuber, no, I did not receive any other information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This information reached you during the night from the 15th to the 16th of April; right?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Right. As I reached headquarters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that you had then organised the defence forces for your village; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, together with the commander, the late Franjo Maric. We organised the defence of the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you also said that nothing had happened during April 16th, 1993; right?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: That's right, in this part, yes. Nothing happened on the 16th of April except for this attack on the hill in the evening of the 16th. That is to say, at our left wing. That is to say, at the zone of responsibility of our battalion, and on the right-hand side near Jardol.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what happened in the area you lived in, in the Lasva Valley area, after April 16th?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: In this part of the zone of responsibility of the 2nd Battalion, in the evening, I think, there was an attack. Yes. Yes, there was an attack on the village of Brdo. On the 17th the Muslims took Brdo. In the area of Stara Bila and Mosunj there were no operations. In Jardol there were some operations by the Muslims towards Jardol, that is to say, towards the Croatian part of this settlement. However, with the exception of the 17th, when the point of Brdo was taken, there weren't any major shifts in our zone of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. One last question, please. At the beginning of this cross-examination you mentioned Vlado Santic, a man who stands accused before this Tribunal. You said that you knew him by sight. Could you please tell us if you knew what Vlado Santic's responsibilities were at the time?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: I did not say that I knew Vlado Santic just in passing, I knew him better than I knew the others. He is distantly related to me. Before the war I know he was employed in the civilian police. I know his parents, I know him personally, a person who, until the war, was certainly an exemplary individual. However, I'm truly not familiar with his involvement in the war itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does the Jokeri unit mean anything to you? Have you heard of this unit?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: I have heard of it. I have heard of it, but I didn't know about it because we were located in a different part of the municipality, and we were mostly dealing with problems within our own area of responsibility, and there was no need for us really to communicate because there weren't any operations there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Kurevija. Your Honour, I'm through.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: I would ask Prosecution Exhibit 344 should be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: No objection? No objection. It is admitted into evidence. Counsel Radovic? Re-examined by Mr. Radovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. The Prosecutor asked you which military units existed, and you said that there was only the Viteska Brigade in the territory of Vitez. I shall now read out to you information on military units from document P343 that you've already had in our hands, but I am not going to ask for this document to be shown to the witness once again, because I don't want to waste time. I'm talking about document 343, that is to say, to all units within the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia, and it is stated specifically Bruno Busic Unit. Did that unit exist in the territory of the municipality of Vitez?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then Ludvig Pavlovic unit. Did that unit exist in the territory of Vitez?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then there was also the units of Vitezovi. Did that unit exist in the territory of the municipality of Vitez?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the Vitezovi? Who actually comprised this unit?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: These were young men who were part of this unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the unit of Darko Kraljevic?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: That's it. That is that unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then the 4th Battalion of the military police of Vitez, did that unit exist in the territory of Vitez?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know that that was the organisation. There was a military police but I don't know about this 4th battalion. I don't know. Probably, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Also, the police administration of Travnik is mentioned in this document. However, it is obvious from this same document that they did not exist in the territory of Vitez obviously. Then I also see that there is a lack of clarity with regard to the distinction between home guard and village guard, and that you yourself seemed to be confusing certain notions related to home guard. If I understood what you said in response to the Prosecutor's questions, you believe home guards to be persons who were mobilised into the Viteska Brigade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you see, this document P341, which was also shown to you, which you had in your hands, the home guard units are established as separate territorial units, not as men that are individually mobilised and sent to an existing brigade.

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: I consider the home guards to be those who were mobilised after the conflict and who were sent to the existing brigade. However, classical home guards, as I said, we can see them only after the war when the regiment was established in 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, that is the important thing I'm asking you about. In Vitez, was there ever, during the war, a special home guard unit that was established, whose members and organisation and command would be separate of the Vitez Brigade?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also saw document P335. That is the report related to mobilisation, and also the list of persons who were mobilised. Did you see who signed this document?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: You are mentioning too many numbers of too many documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, then perhaps could this document be shown to the witness once again so he could see who signed it? Page 2, that's where the signature is.

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: It was signed by the head of the defence department.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was his name?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: His name was Marijan Skopljak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And now tell me who was this document sent to? You can see that on page 1.

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: To the defence administration in Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, what about the defence administration of Vitez and the defence administration of Novi Travnik? What kind of relationship did they have? In the document did the exact data have to be mentioned, or was it possible for the signatory of the document not to abide by these rules?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Of course the data were submitted by the defence office and they were sent to their superiors, that is to say, the Travnik defence administration. It had to be accurate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who guaranteed this with this signature?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: The head of the defence office.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if it were established that these data were not correct, what would have happened to him?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: I imagine that sanctions would have been imposed against him, and he would probably have been replaced and whatever.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And now another question: In passing, you said that the Croatian community from Vitez had some soldiers in the territory of Novi Travnik towards the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: No, I did not say the Croatian community.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you say?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: I said Viteska Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So Viteska Brigade. Let us be specific. I mean, there are so many different names that I tend to be confused. If you can get confused I can get confused too.

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Perhaps I also made an admission.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So tell me, when were the members of the Viteska Brigade in the territory of Novi Travnik? Do you remember the exact date?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Part of the men from the Viteska Brigade were there on the very day of the conflict, the 16th of April, in the area above Novi Travnik, Bistrica and Komusina facing the Serbs. I'm not sure, but I think that these were men from the 1st Battalion of the Viteska Brigade, because the 2nd Battalion had taken over seven days earlier on. So they had replaced us. I think that there were even two platoons of that battalion up there, about 40 men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So from the 1st Battalion; right?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: I think it was 1st Battalion but for sure they belonged to the Viteska Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. But this 1st Battalion, that was the one that theoretically covered Ahmici; right?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know when these men from the 1st Batallion returned to Vitez from the positions near Novi Travnik?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: They returned on the afternoon of the 16th. That is when they came on foot. I think 24 or 25 kilometres they traversed on the foot. They reached our headquarters, as I was there, in view of the events up there at Brdo. They came to our headquarters and they had some tea, they took some refreshments, and then they continued on foot towards their respective homes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Any questions from Counsel Slokovic-Glumac? Yes. Re-examined by Ms. Slokovic-Glumac:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour. Let's see the document shown to you by the Prosecutor once again. You don't need to read it. At the end of '92, you said that you were -- what was your post exactly at the HDZ?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: I was President of the basic organisation in Mali Mosunj. President of the basic organisation in Mali Mosunj. I was elected at the end of '91, and I remained at this post until the beginning of the war. At the beginning of the war, the operation of the party was suspended, so it wasn't active during the conflict.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many HDZ members were there in Mali Mosunj?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Mali Mosunj has a population of 800, so there were about 200. So counting all the people of age, all the people were members who had the right to vote. There were a number of sympathisers, but mostly everybody was a member of the HDZ.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the end of '92, who was the President of the municipal county of HDZ in Vitez? So who was the President of the municipal council of HDZ?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Ante Valenta.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Franjo Kurevija, who you mentioned, what was his post?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: He was the President of the initiating committee of the HDZ, the committee that initiated the establishment of the HDZ. So he was a President of the initiating committee in 1991, and then at the elections the President was -- after the elections was Pero Skopljak, and then he took over from Ante Valenta.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the report from the 20th of January, 1992, it is said that this is a meeting of the county committee, which was expanded with members of the HDZ and its representatives. So because you were only chairman of the HDZ basic organisation, you could not have attended that meeting?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: If I hadn't have come here I wouldn't have found out that I was on that list. I did not attend that meeting, and I could not have done that because of my post, because within the HDZ itself there were 21 or 22 basic organisations. So within a municipal organisation, beside the municipal -- the President of the municipal committee, there were also 21 or 22 other members from Vitez alone, and then you would need to take into account all the other branches.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us who Stipo Krizanac was, what was his post?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: He was a member of the municipal committee. He was maybe some kind of representative. Really, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this is obviously a mistake?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, definitely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we look at these units again, please? According to the what the Prosecutor asked you, you said that out of the military units in Vitez on the day the conflict broke out, or in the period of 1993, there was a part of the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade. That was the Vitez Brigade. How many men did the Vitez Brigade number?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: One hundred and sixty, according to my estimates at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: The Vitez Bogna. The Stjepan Tomasevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When it became the Vitez Brigade, how many people did it number?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Well, around March, when it was being divided, until the beginning of the conflict, there were a few members who joined the active components. So out of the two platoons, when the Vitez battalion came back to Vitez in the zone of our responsibility, the number of manpower grew. So then we had four platoons. If the other battalions grew at the same rate in that region, then according to my estimate, the Vitez Brigade could have had about 320 persons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So with the Vitez Brigade that numbered 300 on the day the conflict broke out, you also said that there were Special Purpose Units, Vitezovi?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, Vitezovi.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many persons were there in Vitezovi?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: I really don't know. I don't know. Maybe about a hundred, but I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were the Vitezovi part of the Vitez Brigade or part of the command territory of Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: No. They were not a part of the Vitez Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they in the structure at all?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this was a unit that was acting independently; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Besides that Special Purpose Unit, Vitezovi, were there any other Special Purpose Units in the region of Vitez?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that there was military police, but you didn't know within what unit it operated.

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, there was military police, but I don't know what its organisation was, within which unit it operated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the Vitez Brigade and the Vitezovi Special Purpose Units, besides these there were no other units in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us if you know that in the course of January of 1993 there were any attacks by the HDZ against Muslim villages in the municipality of Vitez?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether the HVO attacked in the area of Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: No, but I know that the BH army, members of the BH army attacked the Croatian village of Dusina there. So I know about that attack by Muslims against the HVO, but I don't know of any attacks by the HVO against the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Besides the attack in Busovaca, which was carried out by the BH army against the Croatian villages in that area, were there any other conflicts in the course of '93 between the HVO and the BH army in the region of Vitez, up until the breaking out of the conflict on the 16th of April?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: In the region of Vitez I think not. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Except the conflict in Busovaca, were there any conflicts other than that?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: I think, yes, there was one in Uskoplje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but Uskoplje is not part of --

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: No, I don't remember any attacks in that region.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in the region of Lasva Valley, except the conflicts in '93, there were no other incidents that happened until this one that broke out on April 16th?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: No, I don't remember any. If there had been I probably would remember them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said, regarding the home guard units, in response to the Prosecutor's question whether there were any home guard units which were founded based on this decision that he showed you, you stated that you believed that this was not the case.

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Besides the village guards that the Croats had in certain villages, did the Muslims have village guards as well?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know. They probably did, but I really -- I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you don't know how they were established or whether they existed?

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: No, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Counsel Slokovic-Glumac, do you have many more questions?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: No. Thank you very much. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. All right. I assume there is no objection to the witness being released. Mr. Kurevija, thank you so much for coming here to give evidence in court. You may now be released.

utterances.speaker: RUDO KUREVIJA (resumed)
utterances.text: Thank you. (The witness withdrew)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: We will take a 15-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: (The witness entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Could you please make the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon. I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Examined by Ms. Slokovic-Glumac:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good day, Mr. Grebenar. Would you please tell us your name, date of birth, place of birth and where you are living now?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: My name is Dragan Grebenar, born on the 25th of July, 1960 in Poculica in the municipality of Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you live until the war?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: I lived in Poculica in the municipality of Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could we have the aerial map set up again. I didn't see that you had put it away. Could you please indicate on the map for us where Poculica is and could you tell us what are the settlements surrounding Poculica, which community did it belong to? Would you please look at the map behind you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Can I stand up? Poculica is here. The village of Poculica, which is along the highway Vitez-Zenica, the border of the village was there, then it continues onto the village of Prnjavor and the village of Vrhovine. After the elections, this all belonged to one community, so three villages, Poculica, Prnjavor, Vrhovine was one community. That was called Poculica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what was the ethnic structure of the population in the village of Poculica?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: The population of the village of Poculica, according to the census of '91, there were 408 Croats, 328 Muslims in the village of Poculica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the local community? What was the structure of Prnjavor and Vrhovine?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Prnjavor and Vrhovine were 100 per cent Muslim villages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the population of those villages?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: According to these census of '91, there were 284 and 443 Muslims, 284 in Prnjavor and 443 in Vrhovine. So at the local community level there were about 1.055 Muslims and 408 or 409 Croats.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The local community of Poculica borders with the local community of Ahmici; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Yes. A part of the community where the village of Vrhovine is borders on a forest where -- there is the village of Barin Gaj, so this is where these two communities bordered, where the local community of Poculica bordered with the local community of Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the majority population in Poculica was Croatian?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the structure within the village? Were the houses of Muslims and Croats all mixed up or were parts of the village predominantly Muslim or predominantly Croatian?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: As I have already stated, Prnjavor and Vrhovine are exclusively Muslim, while the village of Poculica, the upper part of the village, was mixed. So there were both Muslim and Croats houses there. While the lower part of the village was purely Croatian. So it was populated exclusively by Croats.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The events of '91 and '92, what kind of an effect did they have on Poculica? I am asking you this in order to find out whether village guards began to be formed in Poculica as well.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: The events of '91 and '92, of course, affected any ordinary people in the municipality. As far as any incidents in the village of Poculica, this did not occur. We didn't have any incidents take place. No conflicts. We tried to cooperate, agree with each other, and we managed to do this, maintaining, according to need, or holding, according to need, joint meetings every 10 days. And we tried not to pay any attention to what was happening around us in Ahmici and Travnik, in Busovaca, in other places. We wanted to preserve our peace and continue to live as we had lived until then. Then somebody at some higher level would determine how things were going to turn out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were telling us all of these things now, when you tell us that there were agreements within the village, who reached these agreements?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Yes. There were agreements.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who are you talking about, Muslims and Croats?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Yes, yes, agreements between Muslims and Croats in the village of Poculica, meaning at the level of the local community. So Muslims from the villages of Prnjavor and Vrhovine also had representatives who took part in these talks. I was a representative of the Croatian people, along with some others. These were not closed meetings where only five or six of us attended. No, this was held in a classroom, in an elementary school, and then all the other citizens who were interested could attend. They were usually present. The classroom was usually full of both Croats and Muslims. I have already said that we tried to preserve the peace through these meetings, and I think that it was evident that we succeeded in this, because the incidents that took place around us did not reflect upon our relations in the village, but they did cause increased fear among the people. Then towards the end, even some distrust, but it was all quite within ordinary bounds. So until the 16th I can say that we were one of the better places in our municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were the reasons for these meetings?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Well, exactly what I said, all the events that were taking place around us. So out of this fear that it wouldn't occur to somebody to do something that was inappropriate, either from the Muslim or the Croat side, we tried to organise ourselves at the level of the local community to discuss these matters and to try to see who had weapons from the Muslims and from the Croats. So the goal of these meetings was to maintain the trust and our common life together. And I can say that we were successful in this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you say until the 16th of April there were no problems in the village of Poculica?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: No, none.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Nor any incidents?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: No, there were no incidents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were the village guards organised in the village of Poculica?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Village guards were organised maybe in '92 or maybe -- at the beginning, in March. At that time the village guards began to get organised.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the reason for their establishment?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: The reasons for their establishment were similar to the reasons out of which these joint meetings were held. Fear was slowly creeping in, aggression, Serb aggression against Sarajevo had already begun, and then in the municipality of Vitez or there the majority Serb village of Tolovici also was topical. For those reasons we organised ourselves. We would come out at night a little bit, maintain some controls. There was a larger number of crimes at the level of the municipalities, robberies, so this was done in order to protect the people and property. The village guards at the beginning were not planned, there were no schedules, but it was just out in the evening we would take a walk out through the village at night, a couple of the men and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you said that those village guards were organised at their own initiative in the village by members of certain ethnic groups?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were they armed?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: They were practically not armed. We had a few hunters, a couple of hunters in the village. They had hunting rifles. There were a couple of men who had special guns, so that was the village guard in the beginning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then later on did the number of men taking part in the guard rise?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Yes, with time there was a larger number of men who participated in the guards, and also the number of weapons that they had at their disposal. As time went on, as the war in Bosnia and Herzegovina was getting more intense, people tried, for reasons of personal safety, to obtain weapons in some way or another. Many of them personally for their own money obtained weapons. They purchased them. I know that in my village a lot of people obtained weapons with the departure of Serbs from the village of Tolovici. They were either colleagues, so the Serbs could not cross into Serb territory with their weapons, so they had to leave the weapons. And the fact was that they were very well armed, so a part of the Croatian population, probably part of the Muslim population, obtained their weapons in this way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the Muslims have guards in the village?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. The Muslims also had guards in the village. But after us, in the second half of 1992, after Slimena. I think Slimena occurred in May or June, and after that the Muslims brought in quite a number of weapons from Slimena. I remember seeing on the road that they had small tank trucks and small vehicles. They had rifles that were burnt through the fighting, but they managed to make use of those weapons as well. They organised their own village guards as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there checkpoints in the village?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, there were checkpoints. I think this was after the fall of Jajce -- after the fall of Jajce additional weapons were obtained and checkpoints were organised, village guards. So it wasn't that one group did it without the knowledge of the other, namely, when the Croats set up their own guards, we had a joint meeting where we discussed the need to organise village guards. Then the representatives of the Muslims said that they have nothing to organise these guards with, but they are not opposed to our village guards patrolling the village. But we agreed then that the Croat village guards should go up to the last Croat house in the village, that is to say at the top of the village near the mosque. That is how far the Croat village guards went. They never went into the purely Muslim part of the village, that is to say towards the border with the village of Prnjavor. Also, when the Muslims organised their village guards, we had agreed on the same thing, that they should come to the last Muslim house, that is to say that they did not go into the lower part of the village which was purely Croat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I asked you about these checkpoints in the village.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Oh, yes, yes. These checkpoints too. I already told you, there were different convoys. People were saying that weapons were being smuggled, there was still some Serbs in Zenica, weapons, persons were brought in, and we had a checkpoint that was manned by the Croats in the lower part of the village. The Muslims had a checkpoint at the top, at Vjetrenice. That is at the border between Poculica and that is to say the municipality of Vitez and the municipality of Zenica. They had their own checkpoint there and we had our own. But I must say that we did have a sort of coordination and co-operation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Within the village guards was there a person who was involved in saying who would go on duty where and when and had some kind of control?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. There was some people who were involved in such things earlier on who enjoyed a certain reputation in the village, who were respected by their own people. That is what the situation was like on the Muslim side and that was the situation on our side too. As village guards were established, they took over control, as it were, over these guards, who had weapons, et cetera. So this was on both sides, people on both sides did this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At some point in time were you in charge of the village guards? Did you exercise this kind of control?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I think I was the fourth or the fifth in the village from the Croatian side who took his turn at discharging this duty. I think this was the second half of 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, did you also take part in these talks with the Muslims that you referred to as a way in which problems were resolved in the village?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, did you notice that trenches were being dug, perhaps, around the village?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Well, trench-digging started sometime towards the end of 1992. Muslims were digging trenches at Vjetrenice, that is to say at the borderline between the municipalities and also between the local communities of Poculica and Vjetrenice. And again we talked about this and we asked why this was being done. However, already at that stage it was clear, at least to some of us, that what was being done was not a good thing. And there were some among the Muslims who also thought that this was not necessary. However, the explanation given by those who were doing it was that they were doing this if there were to be some kind of Serb aggression, that they would use it for their guns and for anti-aircraft action, et cetera. So naturally we were satisfied with this explanation and that is the way it was, these trenches were dug and they were up there at Vjetrenice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since you are near Ahmici, the closest village to Ahmici, did you notice that things started changing after the first conflict in Ahmici in October, 1992?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Well, yes. No one was indifferent to what had happened to Ahmici. However, I already said that this did not exactly have any fateful consequences as regards the local community of Poculica. We still had the kind of relationships we had and we managed to overcome this through these discussions that we had at our joint meetings. Naturally, there was a bit more fear and a bit more of a lack of confidence, but all of that for us was at that time within the bounds of the normal. It did not lead to any grave incidents on the territory of the local community.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you notice at that time that as this roadblock was put up and as it was put down that the Muslims from Ahmici withdrew via Poculica?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: No, no, not through the village of Poculica. I didn't notice this. I didn't see this. I didn't see them coming from Ahmici. However, later in the upper part of the village I saw some of this, and I also heard from my colleagues at work, from Vrhovine or Prnjavor, say that they had received some refugees and that they came through Barin Gaj and also through this forest that leaves to Vrhovine that I mentioned. However, I did not see them pass through Poculica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any refugees in Poculica otherwise from other parts of Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Yes. There were refugees in Poculica. I cannot tell you what the exact period was, but even before the fall of Jajce there were refugees from I don't know where. But these refugees were mostly staying in the villages of Prnjavor and Vrhovine, that is to say purely Muslim villages. However, I also noticed in the upper parts of the villages, for example in the house of Kasim Krehic, he had an empty house or one-storey of his house was empty. And there were eight to ten of them, I think. And then as Jajce fell, this number went up considerably so. And practically every house in Prnjavor and Vrhovine had a few refugees, I mean staying with them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you employed in April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Yes, I was employed. I worked in the SPS factory in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From when?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: I had worked in SPS from 1983. I started working there at the end of 1983, in the SPS factory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any people in the village who were part of the active component of the Vitez battalion?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Yes. This was the end of 1992 or the beginning of 1993. I do not know exactly when this was established, but I do know that there were some young men who came to these meetings of ours, that is to say the representatives of the Croatian people, they said that they would not go out for guard duty in the village, that they now belonged to the active component and that they had different obligations, as they put it. What kind of obligations they were referring to, I did not ask because they did not fall under our competencies any more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So they did not do guard duty then?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: No. No, they were not on the village guards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you do on the 15th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: The 15th of April, 1993? It was just like any other day for us, except that things were a bit more tense, because in Zenica, I think the Muslim army attacked the commander of the HVO in Zenica, Totic. We heard about that from people who were coming in from Zenica and passing through. We heard about it in different ways. In the afternoon it was already on television. On that day I was in Vitez. I had some personal matters to attend to, and I went there around 12.00 and I got back around 4.00 p.m. Around 2.00 or 2.30 I met Mr. Zoran Kupreskic and Senad Topoljak. That day they went out of the company. They left work. I didn't even go to work that day. Most of us had unpaid leave of absence. We were all colleagues there at work. We were co-workers. We shared offices, and we naturally talked to one another, we had a drink. They had actually heard something up there at the company, and they asked me whether it was true that this had happened in Zenica. They weren't sure. I said, "Yes, that's what I heard," but I didn't know anything more specific. So we spent about an hour there, an hour, an hour and a half together, and I went home. Actually, we all parted there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that on that day you had not gone to work because there was no need for you to go there to work or why?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Precisely. In the SPS factory I was the foreman. I was in charge of one shift. As all the these things were going on, the volume of work in the company was reduced, and there was a lot less work than normal, and since I had two assistants, we took turns. Every 15 days or so one of us would stay at home. We had only worked with one-third of our labour force, so there was no need for us all to go to work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you went back home, what happened then?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: After I went home, I think that my wife and family told me that they had watched a press conference on TV or something. They saw what had happened in Zenica, and they confirmed that it was true, that these four or five young men were killed, those who were Commander Totic's escorts, and he was apprehended and taken in an unknown direction. So there was fear. I felt an urge to go out and take a walk in the village, and that is exactly what I did. I saw my Muslim neighbours and my Croat neighbours. We were all terrified, and we were all waiting to see what would happen. Both were afraid. How should I put this? However, nothing had any effect on what we were doing. Naturally, we agreed on how our village guard duty would take place that evening, and nothing had indicated anything special, so that day was a pretty regular day, as much as it could have been in that situation and in those times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then what happened in the morning?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Well, in the morning I was awakened around 5.00, perhaps ten minutes before five, by two men who were there in the middle part of the village who were on guard duty in that area, and they said that a lady from the neighbourhood had called them and that her sister had called her before that and told her something to the effect of the following: "Are you a normal person? What is going on? Are you still in Poculica when information is coming in that you will be attacked by the Muslims from Vrhovine, Prnjavor, from the direction of Veternica?"

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the name of this woman who said that her sister had called her?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: That woman's name is Mara Papic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where did her sister call from?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Her sister called from Kratina Mahala. That is a village on the other side of Veternica towards Zume.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened then?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Then I asked whether they had noticed anything. So they said, "Well, no, not really, no. Not while they were on duty." And I said, "Well, never mind. I mean, we received this kind of information from women before and nothing really came out of it." So I saw that they looked a bit afraid too, and I said, "Why don't you wait for a while and I'll get ready and I'll join you, we'll go to Mara's to see." So I went up there with them and I asked Mara who she had actually talked to and what all of this was about. She repeated what they had already conveyed to me, that is to say, that her sister had called her, that she was frightened, that she was crying, and that she was saying, "What's wrong with you people? What are you waiting for? Why don't you leave?" And I said, "Well, I don't know. I don't know anything, but I'll try." I had the number of the headquarters in Vitez, and I said, "I'll try to talk to someone over there. I'll try to find Mario," for example, because I had known Mario from the company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mario who?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Mario Cerkez, because we knew each other from the company. We worked in the same factory. But I don't know, a person who was on duty answered the phone and said Mario was not there and asked me what was going on. I said, "Well, there seems to be some fear around here, because information is coming in from other villages that there might be an attack," and this person said, "I have no idea but I'll try and find Mario and I'll tell him to call you back." I gave Mara's telephone number at that same house, and I asked him to try and find Mr. Mario and to see whether they knew anything. We sat there for a while, we couldn't go away from the phone, and I didn't really know what was wise and what was unwise to do. Some ten minutes or so later the phone rang and Mario was on the phone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did he tell you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: He asked me why I was looking for him and then I told him about this, that I was awakened in such and such a way, and that this information was coming in from the neighbouring village, that we might be attacked, that there would be an offensive launched against us, and I asked him whether he knew anything about it, and then he just asked me whether we patrolled the village during the night. And I said, "Yes. Yes, and these guards are here right now. They are the ones that woke me up." And he said me, "Did you notice anything?" and I said, "No, nothing really. Everything seemed normal." Then he recommended to me that we continue this observation, and that we would talk later if necessary and that I should call him again, and that was it. That is how I concluded my conversation with Mario.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Thank you. We can continue tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. So we adjourn now until tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
